column1: # Game profile of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2, base game v65536 + update v131072). In bring-up
# Nintendo's sead engine (gsys / agl / Phive, Havok, CRIWARE), NintendoWare G3d2 on the Switch 2's NVN2 (Nin_Ounce); SDK 22.2.8.
# Modules main + subsdk0 (NintendoSDK_movie) + sdk. The game is a dump: the RomFS holds one zstd frame per file (".zs"), 186,583 files and 26.24 GB over the update.
# The engine family is the one Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom use (see 01007EF00011E000 and 0100F2C0115B6000), so the host's sead paths apply.

column2: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

column1: # rtld is replaced by the host, so it is not in the module list (the survey's guess said the same: main, subsdk0, sdk)
# The dump's RomFS: the region's language mask names the product revision (111) and, on its fourth line, the build ID of the main the data belongs to
# The game asks for its heap in nninitStartup (main+0x260bb10): it reads nn::os::QueryMemoryInfo and sets
# (total − used − 0xaf200000) & ~2 MB, so with the 6 GB pool below it asks for 3.20 GB (0xcce00000) and the host's heap
# region has to hold that much (the log: "heap 3.20 GB (heap region 4.12 GB)"). The 0xaf200000 it keeps back is the game's
# own "virtual address memory": it maps it in the alias region on demand, so the alias region holds it (plus the SDK's
# address-region node area at its start): the log shows 1.50 GB of the alias region mapped and 0.50 GB of the pool.
# 0x240000000 in all: 4.37 GB alias region + 256 MB stacks + 4.12 GB heap (the heap is what is left of the block).
# The shaders are the engine's: BNSH in the Shader/*.bfsha.zs files (Model, Foliage, SceneMaterial, TerrainGround) and the ApplicationPackage SARC archive, like the other Switch 2 games'

column2: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time shaders
